## 2. Supported Storage Backends

LightRAG requires four storage types: key-value (KV), vector, graph, and document status. The default stores are in-memory databases with local file persistence, suitable only for small-scale testing/evaluation, **not** production. For production, **PostgreSQL is recommended** and can serve all four storage types; MongoDB and OpenSearch are the other single-backend options. Specialized databases: Milvus or Qdrant for vector; Neo4j or Memgraph for graph. [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag) [call-32250a18](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md)

## 3. Differences Between the Available Storage Options

Documented differences:
- **Default in-memory + local file persistence**: simple, zero external dependencies, but explicitly "suitable only for small-scale testing and evaluation, not for production." [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)
- **PostgreSQL**: recommended for production; a single backend can serve all four storage types on its own; suited to large datasets. [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)
- **MongoDB / OpenSearch**: the other single-backend options (each can serve all four types). [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)
- **Milvus / Qdrant**: specialized vector-storage alternatives (vector only). [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)
- **Neo4j / Memgraph**: specialized graph-storage alternatives (graph only). [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)

Key trade-off: single-backend (PostgreSQL/MongoDB/OpenSearch) simplifies operations (one system to back up, monitor, and migrate) versus specialized stores (Milvus/Qdrant/Neo4j/Memgraph), which may offer richer domain features but require operating additional systems and cover only one storage type. The evidence does not quantify performance, consistency, or operational differences beyond production suitability and scope.

## 6. Recommended Production Storage Architecture (Reasoned Recommendation)

**This section is a reasoned recommendation, not a fully verified configuration.** It is separated from documented facts above.

**Recommended:** Use **PostgreSQL as the single backend for all four LightRAG storage types** (KV, vector, graph, document status) in production.

**Rationale:**
- Official documentation recommends PostgreSQL for production deployments with large datasets and states it can serve all four storage types on its own. [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)
- A single backend minimizes operational surface (one backup, one monitoring/alerting target, one migration path, one connection pool to tune) compared with combining specialized stores.
- Avoids the default in-memory/file stores, which are explicitly not for production. [call-32250a18](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag)

**Optional specialization (only if workload justifies added complexity):** add Milvus or Qdrant for vector, or Neo4j/Memgraph for graph, while keeping PostgreSQL for KV and doc-status. This increases operational overhead and is not required by the documentation.

**Caveats / validation needed before adopting:**
- Confirm PostgreSQL connection string, pooling, schema/migrations, and any vector extension requirements (e.g., pgvector) against the current LightRAG docs — not captured in evidence.
- Neon compatibility is unverified; if considering Neon (serverless PostgreSQL), test connection behavior and confirm LightRAG works with it, since LightRAG docs do not mention Neon.
- Resolve the official Docker image question if containerized deployment is required.
- Retrieve the full "Storage Types Supported" page and complete `ProgramingWithCore.md` storage table to confirm exact backend class names and options.
